title: Twelve Clocks

script.text: The country with the most time zones isn't Russia. It's France.

script: Russia has [11|eleven]. The [U.S.|U S], counting tiny islands, also has [11|eleven].
Because France doesn't stop at Europe.
There's French Guiana, in South America.
Guadeloupe and Martinique, in the Caribbean.
New Caledonia, French Polynesia, and Wallis and Futuna, out in the Pacific.
Its clocks run from [UTC−10|U T C minus ten], in Tahiti, to [UTC+12|U T C plus twelve], in Wallis.
It gets stranger. France's longest land border isn't with Spain.

script.text: It's with Brazil, through French Guiana.

script: And on the island of Saint Martin, France borders the Netherlands.
Count [Adélie|Adelie] Land, in Antarctica, and France claims a [13th|thirteenth] zone.
Spread that wide, somewhere in France, the sun is always up.
sources: Sun-always-up: own calculation, minimum solar altitude over French territories across 2026 = 22 deg
